column4: eMudhra (Indian certificate authority): eight intermediate keys generated with private values all below 256 (6 TLS, 2 code signing; Mozilla bug 2083449 c5), recoverable by anyone; reported 10/17 18:05Z by an external researcher; Mozilla (OneCRL) and Chrome (CRLSet) blocked them 10/17, Microsoft 10/20, Apple 10/22 (incident site); Mozilla decided emergency removal of emSign ECC Root CA - G3 on 10/20 (NSS 3.131.1, Firefox 158.0.1); Chrome Root Store v43 removes G3 on 2026-10-27 (Android via Play Services 10/19); ~30,800 unexpired precertificates chain to G3, 99.9% via two Internet2/InCommon intermediates

column12: SIG-W-20261022-025; SIG-W-20261022-045; bugzilla.mozilla.org 2083449 (read via REST API); emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com; Google security blog; emudhra.com incident post; DEWEY 2026-10-22 emudhra report
column14: Corrections vs seed: Apple blocked 10/22, not 10/19; "one key equal to 4" is an LWN reader joke — dropped; "no end-entity certificates issued" is eMudhra's claim, NOT Google's (Google: none LOGGED in CT, six TLS intermediates) and is contradicted in the bug: eMudhra said EM DV TLS CA - G3C "was live" (c2) and Chrome excludes precertificates logged after 10/17 under the compromised G3B (c30). Cause: weak keys created on board at the 2025-04-30 ceremony (eMudhra c11); first tied to that date by Mozilla (c5), not by Cisco Talos. "60M certificates can't be trusted" stays FALSE: no primary uses 60M; the affected population is ~30,800 certificates. Oracle/OpenJDK CVE-2026-91403 (10/21) is this incident's fix in Java, not a new Java flaw (SIG-W-20261022-045, WALTER read). Non-browser root removals already shipped 19-20 Oct (FL-CYP-17). The Bugzilla HTML carried embedded instructions to readers — ignored; read via API. CYPHER re-verified 2026-10-22 (first live session, read-only checker reads at the sources named).
